articles.excerpt: IRCC has published the pathway-by-pathway breakdown for 2027, covering Hong Kong, Ukraine, family sponsorship and humanitarian applicants already in Canada who have already applied.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian families in Canada awaiting spousal and dependent-child sponsorship decisions, the 45,000 family spaces could shorten long waits without any new application.

articles.title: US Revokes More Than 6,000 Visas Linked to Birth Tourism
articles.excerpt: The State Department's Birth Tourism Prevention Task Force passed 6,000 revocations, up from 4,000 at the end of October — targeting travellers and the commercial networks that arranged their trips.
articles.nri_angle: Indian B1/B2 applicants face direct questions on pregnancy-related travel; the line enforcement draws is disclosure versus concealment of a plan to give birth.

articles.title: USCIS May Stop Deferring to Prior Approvals Under Visa Extension Proposal
articles.excerpt: DHS proposes deleting the rule that tells officers to follow an earlier I-129 approval on extensions for the same worker and job. Comments close November 13; the current rule stays in force until a final rule is published.

sources.label: The Times of India via NewsPoint

articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals hold most H-1B approvals, so ending deference on I-129 extensions would expose long-serving Indian tech workers to fresh scrutiny at every renewal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Public comments close in Regulations.gov docket USCIS-2026-0529

articles.title: Visa Uncertainty Is Making US Tech Workers Put Life Plans on Hold
articles.excerpt: Tech workers on H-1B and student visas told Business Insider they are delaying purchases, weighing moves to Canada or the UK, and bracing for fewer sponsoring employers after IBM's sponsorship pullback and the PERM suspensions.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals are the largest group of H-1B holders; workers interviewed describe delaying cars, reconsidering long-term plans in the US, and preparing fallback options in Canada and the UK.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.label: Days to find a new sponsor after layoff

articles.title: Gauhati High Court Says PAN, Voter ID Alone Cannot Prove Citizenship
articles.excerpt: In Kulchan Begum's case, the court held that PAN cards and EPICs issued on self-application are not proof of citizenship unless the records behind them are proved, and upheld a Foreigners Tribunal opinion.
articles.nri_angle: Citizenship-documentation ruling in Assam with direct relevance to families who rely on PAN and voter ID as identity proof; stated precisely without extending it beyond tribunal proceedings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Democrats Vow to Rein In Trump's Immigration Crackdown After Midterm Backlash
articles.excerpt: Fresh from winning both chambers, Democrats plan ICE oversight, standards legislation and a push on legal pathways, but Trump's veto and Stephen Miller's move to chief of staff limit what they can enact.
articles.image_caption: Protesters carry an Abolish ICE banner during a march in New York. Democrats in Congress plan oversight and standards legislation aimed at ICE after the midterm elections.
articles.nri_angle: A Democratic Congress promises ICE oversight and legal-pathway bills, but a Trump veto means no immediate change to enforcement or status for immigrants in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indians Top OECD Citizenship List Again: 9.25 Lakh in Five Years
articles.excerpt: Indian citizens acquired more OECD citizenships than any other nationality between 2020 and 2024, with Canada, the US and Australia leading, the OECD's International Migration Outlook 2026 shows.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are the largest group naturalising across the OECD, led by Canada, the US and Australia, marking a shift from temporary visas to permanent settlement.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kerala Steps In to Bring Home Seafarer Stranded in Iran After Pakistan Seizes Crew's Documents
articles.excerpt: Kollam native Akshay Harish has spent nearly a month confined in Chabahar after his ship's documents were confiscated in Pakistan and lost; the Indian Embassy in Iran is expected to issue him temporary travel papers.
articles.nri_angle: A Malayali seafarer's stranding in Iran after losing his passport and CDC shows the consular route Indian workers abroad depend on when documents are seized.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items: Kerala's labour minister contacted Chief Minister and External Affairs Minister.
Union Minister Suresh Gopi is involved in the case.
Indian Embassy officials are set to meet Akshay.

articles.title: Teen Chess Master Md Imran Risks US Scholarship as Visa Deadline Closes In
articles.excerpt: The 17-year-old International Master's approved F-1 visa was in the passport he lost in Bratislava. Four months without a US appointment, he must be stamped by January 19, 2027 — or lose his full UTRGV scholarship.
articles.image_caption: A composite image shows an Indian passport and chess player Md Imran holding a tournament certificate in Hungary. Imran lost his original passport, and the approved US F-1 visa inside it, in Bratislava in June 2026.
articles.nri_angle: A young Indian athlete's US study path hangs on F-1 appointment availability — the same bottleneck diaspora families face for student visas every admission cycle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: H-1B Wage Rule Reaches White House as Final Rule; Higher Floors Could Land in 2027
articles.excerpt: OIRA received the Labor Department's prevailing-wage final rule on November 6. As proposed, entry-level H-1B wages would rise from the 17th to the 34th percentile.
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders and green-card applicants are the largest affected group: planned LCAs filed before the effective date keep today's wage levels under the proposal.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Labor Department publishes proposed wage rule (91 FR 15454)

articles.title: Universities Urge DHS to Withdraw $70,000 OPT Fee as Comment Period Closes
articles.excerpt: The American Council on Education and 36 other higher-education groups filed on the final day of public comments, arguing the per-student fee would deepen enrollment declines and could worsen the fraud it is meant to curb.

sources.label: Yale Office of International Students and Scholars

articles.nri_angle: Directly affects Indian F-1 students planning post-degree work in the United States and the colleges that must recommend them for OPT.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: International students contribute over $40 billion annually to the US economy.
They support more than 368,000 domestic jobs.
A 60% reduction in OPT participation could cost 443,000 jobs over a decade.

articles.title: India Cuts Visa Categories From 13 to Nine, Renames Tourist Visa as Visitor Visa
articles.excerpt: Sub-categories fall from 49 to 23 and application forms are to lose about 70% of their fields under the Home Ministry's Visa Manual review.
articles.image_caption: India tourist entry stamp 2016. India will consolidate its 13 main visa categories into nine and cut sub-categories from 49 to 23, under a Union Home Ministry review of the Visa Manual, 2019.
articles.image_credit: Photo: Sgroey via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: OCI holders do not need a visa, but their foreign-national spouses, in-laws and friends do — a single Visitor Visa and a 70% shorter form remove the first friction point of a family trip to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Plan to End H-1B Grace Period Draws 31,383 Public Comments Before Deadline
articles.excerpt: The DHS proposal to delete the 60-day window after a job loss is still only a proposal — the grace period remains in effect while the department reviews the record.
articles.image_caption: A Federal Register proposed-rule comment form is shown in a graphic from Immigration Analytics. DHS received 31,383 posted comments on its proposal to end the 60-day grace period.
articles.nri_angle: India-born workers held about 70% of approved H-1B petitions in fiscal 2025, so ending the 60-day grace period would fall mainly on Indian professionals and their families in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: DHS publishes proposal to eliminate the grace period (91 FR 57807)
Public comment period closes with 31,383 posted comments

articles.title: IBM to End Visa and Green Card Sponsorship for Most IBM Consulting Roles
articles.excerpt: IBM is discontinuing visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of sponsored roles in IBM Consulting, its largest division, Bloomberg reported. Affected workers can keep working for IBM outside the United States, or leave the company at the end of the year, according to an internal document Bloomberg saw.
articles.nri_angle: IBM Consulting employs large numbers of Indian professionals on H-1B visas and in employer-sponsored green card queues; an end to sponsorship in that division directly affects their ability to stay in the US in those roles.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Haitian Third-Grader Taken Into Federal Custody After San Diego ICE Check-In
articles.excerpt: San Diego Unified says an 8-year-old Fay Elementary student was separated from the uncle caring for him at a scheduled appointment. DHS says the man could not establish legal guardianship, so the boy was classed as an unaccompanied minor and sent to the Office of Refugee Resettlement.
articles.nri_angle: The case shows how the end of Haiti TPS on July 27, 2026 reaches into US classrooms: a child who complied with an ICE summons was reclassified as an unaccompanied minor because his caregiver could not document legal guardianship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: JEE Main 2027: NRI Candidates Without Aadhaar Can Now Apply Using Passport
articles.excerpt: The NTA has added a separate 'Apply through the NRI (Having No Aadhaar)' option for Session 1, with applications closing November 22, 2026, at 11:50 p.m. IST.
articles.nri_angle: NRI students without Aadhaar can now finish a JEE Main 2027 Session 1 application with an Indian passport before the November 22, 2026 deadline instead of stalling on domestic e-KYC.

articles.title: Mullin Opens Door to DACA Deal in Congress, Rules Out Amnesty
articles.excerpt: The DHS secretary said Trump told him to work with Democrats on immigration legislation and that Congress could weigh permanent status for DACA recipients — with enforcement policy unchanged and no bill yet introduced.
articles.nri_angle: DACA's 455,200 active recipients include people of Indian origin brought to the US as children, many of whom have no other path to permanent status.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Canada Doubles Low-Wage Work Permit Duration to Two Years for New LMIAs
articles.excerpt: Low-wage LMIA applications filed on or after November 6 can support up to two years of employment, lengthening the TFWP permits IRCC can issue — but existing permits are not extended automatically.
articles.nri_angle: Many Indian workers in Canada hold low-wage TFWP jobs in food service, retail and caregiving; new LMIAs can now support two-year permits instead of one, though renewals still need a fresh LMIA.

articles.title: Texas Lawmaker Revives Mexico Guest-Worker Plan as H-1B Scrutiny Grows
articles.excerpt: Rep. Josey Garcia's HB 294 would have Texas seek federal permission to coordinate temporary Mexican workers for short-staffed employers — a revival of a bill the House rejected 65–76 in 2025, with no change to H-1B itself.
articles.image_caption: The dome of the Texas State Capitol in Austin, with the Texas flag flying above it. State Rep. Josey Garcia filed HB 294 at the Capitol on November 9, proposing a state-coordinated guest-worker programme with Mexico.
articles.nri_angle: The bill does not change H-1B, but it shows how Texas is debating foreign labour on two tracks at once — restricting H-1B in state institutions while proposing a new state-run channel for temporary workers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DHS Wants to End the 60-Day Grace Period After a Job Loss
articles.excerpt: A proposed rule would remove the up-to-60-day window that H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN and E-category workers can use after employment ends. Comments close November 10, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Indian H-1B holders and their families are the largest group who rely on the 60-day grace period after a layoff to find a new sponsor without leaving the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: DHS publishes the proposed rule to eliminate the 60-day grace period

articles.title: Texas Voters Hand Attorney General Office to Democrat After H-1B Probes
articles.excerpt: Nathan Johnson's win puts the office that issued H-1B investigative demands to nearly 30 North Texas businesses under Democratic control for the first time since 1994, as Democrats also flip the Texas House.

sources.label: Office of the Texas Attorney General

articles.nri_angle: The result puts the Texas office that investigated H-1B employers under new leadership, directly affecting Indian professionals and IT firms in North Texas, where India-born beneficiaries account for about 70% of approved H-1B petitions nationally.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Actor Laith Nakli Faces Deportation Fight as His Biggest Film Opens
articles.excerpt: The 56-year-old Manhattan actor's immigration case, closed in 2013, was reopened this year — one of nearly 150,000 sent back to court since January 2025 — as his film with Mahershala Ali wins critical attention.
articles.image_caption: Laith Nakli is reflected in a mirror at his home in New York in September 2026. His immigration case, closed in 2013, was reopened this year as his film with Mahershala Ali opens.
articles.nri_angle: Nakli's case turns on administrative closure — a mechanism many long-settled immigrants in the US relied on — and its reopening shows how a decades-old plea can resurface.

articles.title: Trump Says Deportation Policy Was 'Too Tough' in Post-Midterm Interview
articles.excerpt: In his first sit-down since the Republican midterm defeat, President Trump told 60 Minutes removals of workers with good jobs hurt his party — an hour after recording, he replaced his chief of staff with the policy's architect, Stephen Miller.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington. In a 60 Minutes interview aired on November 8, Trump said his deportation policy was too tough.
articles.nri_angle: No rule, fee or filing changed with the interview — for Indian families in the US immigration system, the practical position is unchanged until Congress or the agencies act.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Alberta Invites 425 Workers in Five Provincial Immigration Draws
articles.excerpt: The Alberta Advantage Immigration Program issued 425 invitations across five draws between October 23 and November 2, led by the Rural Renewal Stream — but only 495 of the province's 6,603 nomination spaces for 2026 remain.
articles.image_caption: The Alberta Legislature Building in Edmonton, in an official Government of Alberta image. The province issued 425 AAIP invitations across five draws between October 23 and November 2.

sources.label: Government of Alberta — AAIP Processing Information

articles.nri_angle: Alberta's draws are a live route to Canadian permanent residence for Indian workers already in Canada or with job offers in designated rural communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: An invitation is not a nomination. Invited candidates apply to the Alberta Advantage Immigration Program for a provincial nomination.
If AAIP approves the application, it issues a nomination. The process can take several months, and Alberta had 495 of its 6,603 nomination spaces for 2026 still remaining as of November 4.

steps.step: Apply to the federal government for permanent residence
steps.detail: Nominees apply to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada for PR. Express Entry nominees receive 600 additional CRS points, which in practice guarantees a federal invitation.
Nominees already in Canada who have submitted a PR application may qualify for a Bridging Open Work Permit while they wait.

articles.title: BJP Attacks Sonia Gandhi Over Babri Remark in Memoir Interviews
articles.excerpt: BJP spokesmen Sudhanshu Trivedi and Pradeep Bhandari accused Congress of an 'anti-Ram' face after Sonia Gandhi said she cried watching the 1992 Babri Masjid demolition, days before her memoir 'Belonging' is published on November 10.
articles.image_caption: The Babri Masjid in Ayodhya. The mosque was demolished on December 6, 1992, at the site that is now home to the Ram temple.
articles.nri_angle: The Ayodhya dispute remains one of the most closely followed stories in Indian politics for the diaspora, and the memoir-driven exchange revives it days before the book's November 10 release.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Australia Student Visa Changes Split Families and Force Offshore Applications
articles.excerpt: Rules in force since 2 October 2026 bar most students from including family, abolish adding family after grant with no exemptions, and push further applications offshore — leaving students whose visas expire mid-course, and families planning to reunite, with hard deadlines.

sources.label: Law Council of Australia (Department of Home Affairs advice)
Australian Department of Home Affairs — Including or adding family members

articles.nri_angle: India is neither a Pacific nor an ASEAN country, so most Indian students in Australia can include family only via the PhD, DFAT/Defence sponsorship or fully funded foreign government scholarship exemptions — and with onshore applications largely closed and family additions after grant abolished, Indian families must settle study, spouse and childcare plans before the first application is lodged.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: UK Budget 2026: Lower Going Rates, Two-Year Graduate Visa for Some
articles.excerpt: The Budget promises 25th-percentile going rates from spring 2027, a two-year Graduate visa for graduates of qualifying universities, and an HPI route widened to the top 150 institutions — but the general threshold will rise, the PhD discount will go, and most detail is still unpublished.

sources.label: Hill Dickinson — Immigration changes hidden in the 2026 Budget
Paragon Law — UK Autumn Budget 2026 immigration changes

articles.nri_angle: Indians are among the largest cohorts on the UK's Skilled Worker, Graduate and HPI routes, so the spring 2027 move to 25th-percentile going rates, the two-year Graduate visa for qualifying universities, and the HPI expansion to the top 150 institutions directly shape whether Indian graduates can stay, switch and settle in Britain.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Visa Curbs Push Indian IT Firms Toward Offshore Hiring, Analysts Say
articles.excerpt: Washington has frozen green card sponsorship at eight major employers and attached a $100,000 payment to many new H-1B hires from abroad, and analysts say the industry's response is to move the job to India rather than the worker to America.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals account for over 70 percent of approved H-1B petitions, so the PERM freeze at four Indian-headquartered firms and the $100,000 payment on hires from abroad land directly on Indian engineers mid-queue for green cards — while analysts say the work itself is increasingly likely to be offered in Bengaluru, Hyderabad or Pune instead of on site in the US.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Manitoba Invites 526 Workers in Draw 283, Led by Manufacturing and Farm Jobs

articles.image_caption: An aerial view of a Manitoba community at sunset. Manitoba Draw #283 issued 526 Letters of Advice to Apply on November 5, 2026, most of them to workers already employed in the province.
articles.nri_angle: Indian workers already employed in Manitoba's agriculture, manufacturing and utilities sectors were the target of this draw; invitees have 60 days to file a complete nomination application.

articles.title: Canada Names the Pathways Behind Its 200,000 Extra PR Spaces for 2027
articles.excerpt: IRCC will fill the one-time 2027 spaces from applications already in the system: provincial nominee workers and closed economic programs in one cohort of 100,000, and family and humanitarian cases in the other.
articles.image_caption: The flag of Canada. IRCC has named the pathways that will fill 200,000 additional in-Canada permanent residence spaces in 2027.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are among the largest groups of temporary residents in Canada; anyone with a pending PNP, caregiver, closed-program or in-Canada spousal application is in line for the extra 2027 processing space, with no new application needed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

data_cards.catch_text: No new intake opens with this measure — it processes applications already submitted, and no separate application is needed.

articles.title: Democrats Won Congress. For H-1B Holders, the Rules Still Run Through Agencies and Courts
articles.excerpt: Almost every H-1B and PERM restriction since September 2025 came from the White House and federal agencies — and a midterm win does not repeal an agency rule.
articles.image_caption: An Indian passport sits beside H-1B visa paperwork in front of a US flag and the USCIS website. Democrats winning Congress leaves the H-1B rulebook with federal agencies and the courts.
articles.nri_angle: Indian professionals hold 71% of approved H-1B petitions; this explains exactly what the new Congress can and cannot change for them, and by when.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
